title: K-flatness of Hom from a bounded finite-projective ring complex
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and regard A-modules as sheaves on the bottom-topology one-object ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Let P,Q be cochain complexes of these sheaves. Suppose there are integers a,b such that P^n is zero for n<a or b<n, each module P^n at the unique object is finite projective over A, and Q is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then the shared Hom complex Hom_A^\bullet(P,Q) [def-pur-hom-complex] is K-flat.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: Evaluation on the unique object identifies sheaves, sheaf tensor products, and internal Hom with modules, tensor products, and linear Hom. The bottom topology imposes no extra sheaf condition, and the slice over the unique object has one object up to unique isomorphism. Form the dual P^vee in reversed degrees with its usual dual differential. For each finite projective P^i, evaluation Hom(P^i,A) tensor M -> Hom(P^i,M) is invertible: use coordinate evaluation for a finite free module and restrict it and its inverse along the splitting of P^i as a summand. Since P is bounded, each Hom degree contains finitely many nonzero factors. These evaluation maps identify Hom(P,Q) with Tot(P^vee tensor Q); the dual differential and Koszul sign give exactly d_Q f - (-1)^n f d_P.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: P^vee is bounded with finite-projective, hence flat, terms. For every acyclic F, Tot(F tensor P^vee) is acyclic by the bounded-above flat-complex lemma, applied to the evaluated module complexes.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: Associativity of tensor and its Koszul totalization signs identify Tot(F tensor Tot(P^vee tensor Q)) with Tot(Tot(F tensor P^vee) tensor Q). There are only finitely many P^vee factors, so the rearrangement of direct sums is valid even when F and Q are unbounded. K-flatness of Q makes the latter complex acyclic. Transport across the two chain isomorphisms and the exact one-object evaluation equivalence; this gives acyclicity of Tot(F tensor Hom(P,Q)) for every acyclic F, exactly the K-flat predicate.
